Article Title: CCPA penalises Amazon, Flipkart, JioMart for selling unregistered herbicide
Article Text:
Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart, for selling and advertising an unregistered agrochemical product, Cyclosinone Herbicide.Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed as a granular weed-control product used to prevent and eliminate broadleaf and grassy weeds in lawns, gardens and agricultural fields.In separate orders issued recently, the consumer watchdog directed the e-commerce marketplaces to immediately discontinue the false and misleading advertisements and conduct a self-audit of their platforms to identify and remove products that violate the law or pose a risk to consumers’ life and safety.The CCPA initiated proceedings after the department of agriculture and farmers’ welfare forwarded a complaint it had received from the Crop Care Federation of India (CCFI) regarding the sale and advertisement of the unregistered herbicide through e-commerce and digital media platforms.During the investigation, the agriculture department informed CCPA that the import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution and use of insecticides and pesticides are regulated under the Insecticides Act, 1968, and the Insecticides Rules to safeguard human beings and animals from potential risks.The department told the authority that no chemical named Cyclosinone is included in the Schedule to the Insecticides Act. However, a product marketed as “Cyclosinone Herbicide” was being sold through online platforms without disclosing the chemical name of its active ingredient or its composition.“It is currently being marketed illegally because it bypasses the mandatory safety, bio-efficacy, quality and legal checks required under the Insecticides Act,” the department said in its submission to CCPA.The authority rejected the e-commerce companies’ argument that they could not be held responsible for products listed by third-party sellers. The CCPA said online marketplaces cannot disown their statutory obligation to protect consumers and are required to exercise due diligence to prevent the sale of products that are illegal or hazardous.
Article Summary: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart. Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed as a granular weed-control product used to prevent and eliminate broadleaf and grassy weeds.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday paid tribute to former prime minister Manmohan Singh on his birth anniversary, remembering his long public life and service to the nation."Tributes to our former prime minister Dr Manmohan Singh Ji on his birth anniversary. He spent many years in public life and served the nation with dedication," PM Modi said in a post on X.Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) chairperson Sonia Gandhi and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi also paid floral tributes to the former prime minister on his birth anniversary.Sharing a post on X, Rahul Gandhi said, "On the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh ji, I pay my humble respects to him. With his humility, integrity, and foresight, he gave a new direction to the country's economy and social justice. His historic decisions and invaluable contributions to the making of India will forever continue to guide us."Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also paid tribute to Singh saying, "I offer my humble respects. As a skilled economist and successful politician, Dr Manmohan Singh ji imparted extraordinary momentum to India's development and elevated the nation's prosperity to new heights.""Through his visionary and inclusive economic policies, he enriched every section of society.Dr Manmohan Singh ji's unprecedented contributions to the country's development will always be remembered. I pay homage to his memories," he added.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also remembered the former prime minister, saying, "We remember with profound respect the extraordinary contribution of former Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh to India’s nation-building. A visionary statesman, his landmark economic reforms transformed India’s growth trajectory, created new opportunities and helped lift millions out of poverty. His humility, integrity and wisdom defined his public life. ""He led with quiet dignity and compassion, placing inclusive growth and the welfare of the most vulnerable at the heart of governance. The rights-based framework of his government remains an enduring testament to this vision. On his birth anniversary, we pay our heartfelt homage to a statesman whose legacy of honest public service, inclusive development and transformative reforms will continue to inspire generations," he added.Manmohan Singh was born on September 26, 1932, in Gah, in present-day Pakistan, then part of undivided India. He died in New Delhi on December 26, 2024.Singh became India's 14th prime minister on May 22, 2004, and returned for a second consecutive term on May 22, 2009. He served as prime minister until 2014.Before becoming prime minister, Singh served as Union finance minister from 1991 to 1996. During his tenure, India introduced a wide-ranging programme of economic reforms that reshaped the country's economy and earned international recognition.Singh's public life spanned several decades, during which he held key positions in government and played a significant role in shaping India's economic policy.
Article Summary: Singh became India's 14th prime minister on May 22, 2004, and returned for a second consecutive term in 2009. He served as prime minister until 2014. During his tenure, India introduced a wide-ranging programme of economic reforms that reshaped the country's economy.

Article Title: 'No hard feelings': US on India's stern warning over Russia Sanctions Act
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The United States on Saturday said that it was looking to meet India's massive energy needs, days after US President Donald Trump signed the 'Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026', which authorises him to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries buying Russian oil and gas."We are looking to also become a huge source of India's energy needs. We're increasing our hydrocarbon exports,” a senior US state department official told news agency PTI.“The demands are great, and the needs for oil are there. We are looking for alternatives. But I would say before even the war, India had been looking to diversify when it came to energy for a long time. It's not a new concept. We just need to expedite it faster,” he added.The US official also played down New Delhi's warning over the contentious law and said that India's response was expected after the US Congress took a pretty hard approach, especially publicly.“India has been looking for a long time to diversify its energy sources. They're a country that has massive energy needs,” the official told PTI.“You had members of Congress calling out India in particular, so of course India has to respond.We understand that. They have a domestic constituency, as do we. Like, there are no sort of hard feelings on any of that kind of activity," he added.Last week, the ministry of external affairs warned the US of the legislation’s potential impact on the US-India relationship.“This issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side,” the ministry said.The official said that the new act gave President Trump a new tool in his toolbox.“That doesn't necessarily mean he deploys it tomorrow, but he has the opportunity to. His focus is on ending this war. It's been something he campaigned on and something he's been dedicated to from the beginning,” he said.“We're looking for our friends, especially like India, to help support that effort. But I think you'll have to stay tuned on how the bill gets implemented. But there is a broad national security waiver, so you can imagine also the president, there's a scenario, the president uses that as well,” he added."Now, with President Trump's incredibly successful operation in Venezuela, we are moving into a better position that countries like India are going to be able to get access to that market,” he added.
Article Summary: U.S. looking to become a huge source of India's energy needs, says state department official. US President Donald Trump signed the 'Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' last week. New Delhi warned the US of the legislation’s potential impact on the US-India relationship.

CBI on Thursday arrested Abhishek Kumar, a key accused in the Mahadev online betting and gambling case in which Enforcement Directorate (ED) has claimed that the perpetrators of the illegal activities have so far generated and laundered proceeds of crime of more than Rs 94,000 crore.Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI immediately after he arrived at Hyderabad airport from Dubai. He was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni - both continue to operate the gambling network from the UAE and other jurisdictions.Kumar coordinated various panels in the Mahadev network and was responsible for collecting funds and acquiring immovable assets in Dubai out of ill-gotten proceeds of crime, a CBI spokesperson said. He has been taken to Raipur and produced before a special court for police remand. So far, seven Red Corner Notices and two extradition requests have been pending against other accused.The Mahadev online betting and gambling app is still active and proceeds of crime of Rs 94,000 crore have been generated so far by the accused, who are in Dubai, ED has said in its latest chargesheet in the case. More than Rs 1,000 crore has been invested in Indian share markets through foreign portfolio investments (FPIs), the agency said.It estimated that in the last few years, the accused generated more than Rs 11,000 crore annually from illegal online gambling and betting activities.Based on analysis of various seized digital evidence and statements of several accused, ED said that "it can be estimated that proceeds of crime worth Rs 11,400 crore (approx) must have been generated by illegal operations of Mahadev online book every year". The gambling network has been running since 2019."As per latest findings, Mahadev app is still running a huge number of panels. Estimated proceeds of crime generated by the app is around Rs 75,000-80,000 crore during the last seven years," ED has said. In addition, it said other illegal apps run by the syndicate like Skyexchange.com and Lotus365.com have generated proceeds of crime of over Rs 14,000 crore."A majority of the proceeds of crime was layered and transferred to the promoters based in Dubai," ED stated.The agency has so far attached assets worth over Rs 2,000 crore linked to various accused. The agency said the above estimation of proceeds of crime is only a provisional figure and is likely to go up.
Article Summary: Abhishek Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI. He was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni. Kumar was responsible for collecting funds and acquiring immovable assets in Dubai out of ill-gotten proceeds of crime.

Article Title: Centre pleads for prospective effect of SC creamy layer ruling
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Facing the task of implementing Supreme Court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for OBC reservation from the retrospective date of 2012, Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it.The court had in March held that the income of parents could not be the sole criterion to determine the creamy layer of a candidate for exclusion from OBC reservation, and status and category of a parent's job had to be considered with an 'income/wealth test' as an additional criterion. It made the verdict implementable from 2012, when the case was first filed.In a written note filed by additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, govt submitted that the retrospective application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the time and create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression."The retrospective implementation of the present judgement would create changes in candidates' service and cadre allocation... as it would affect the services of persons appointed on the basis of CSE-2012 onward and cause a cascading effect among civil servants... The aforementioned cascading effect will impact not only OBC candidates but also reverberate across all categories including (unreserved category) of the civil services," the note said.Govt said a reasonable time of two years should be given to it to undertake the necessary exercise of establishing equivalence of posts, after consulting all the stakeholders and formulating a uniform policy/mechanism for determination of OBC creamy layer status."Union of India is only praying for a limited deferral of the operationalisation of the law laid down by this hon'ble court for a period of two years so that the competing rights can be adjusted consistent with the administrative contingencies and an effective equivalence exercise is carried out," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for OBC reservation from retrospective date of 2012. Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it. Court had in March held that the income of parents could not be the sole criterion to determine the creamy layer of a candidate for exclusion.

Article Title: NALSAR students screen Umar Khalid documentary after screenings cancelled at IIIT-Hyderabad, NLSIU
Article Text:
The screening was a private event restricted to students.

Prisoner No. 626710 is Present

Hyderabad: The screening of Umar Khalid’s documentary,, which was cancelled at the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad (IIIT-H), and National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, was held at NALSAR University of Law in the city on Wednesday evening. A group of students who independently organised the “solidarity screening” said it was held to offer an opportunity “to engage directly with the film’s questions about rights, accountability and the human cost of prolonged incarceration, while expressing solidarity with those affected by these failures of the justice system”.The screening was a private event restricted to students.“The film raises urgent concerns about the delay in the justice system, and about undertrial prisoners being kept in custody for years without their trials even beginning,” one of the students told TOI via email. “When a person remains imprisoned for six years without trial, the delay itself becomes a serious denial of justice. Law cannot, and should not, be used as a tool of violence without convictions. The process cannot become the punishment,” the email added.NALSAR students have called on student bodies across universities to organise similar screenings of the documentary.The documentary has not been certified by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC).The board has stated that screening an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been obtained.Last week, the screening at IIIT-H was cancelled after the CBFC flagged the issue on X. The institute later said that the proposed event had not been organised or authorised by its management. At NLSIU, too, the event, which was initially postponed, was later cancelled after organisers said they faced threats of criminal action, intimidation, doxxing and other forms of harassment., directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, is a documentary about Khalid, tracing his journey from student activist to his arrest in 2020 and subsequent incarceration.Meanwhile, NALSAR vice-chancellor, Prof Srikrishna Deva Rao, said, “NALSAR University of Law did not authorise screening of the documentary film Prisoner No 626710 on its campus. No official permission for the same was given to anybody by any University authority,”
Article Summary: The screening was a private event restricted to students. NALSAR students have called on student bodies across universities to organise similar screenings. The documentary has not been certified by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) The board has stated that screening an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been obtained.

Article Title: In a first, waste plastic mixed with bitumen in pilot test section of NH-44
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a first for the road sector, govt has used waste plastic as a wet mix with bitumen to lay a bituminous highway stretch, a move that is likely to reduce imports of the key construction material while addressing the growing problem of plastic waste.On Thursday, a pilot test section was laid on the main carriageway of NH-44 in Jhansi. Officials associated with the pilot said the technology has potential to reduce conventional bitumen consumption by around 4%, lowering demand for a material that India largely imports to meet domestic requirements. They added that the modified bitumen could cost around 20% less than conventional bitumen.The waste plastic wet-process technology for producing premium-quality Waste Plastic Modified Bitumen (W-PMB 76-10) has been developed by IIT (BHU), Varanasi, under a research programme funded by the ministry of road transport and highways. The performance of the pilot stretch will be monitored by IIT (BHU) to assess its long-term engineering performance and field suitability, officials said.India generates around 25,000 tonne of plastic waste every day. Until now, waste plastic has been used in road construction only as a dry mix with aggregates while laying the bituminous layer. The new method mixes processed waste plastic directly with bitumen before it is laid, making it the first such pilot on a national highway.Officials said the technology offers multiple benefits, including the value-added reuse of waste plastic through a scientifically controlled process and improved rut resistance of bituminous mixes under high ambient temperatures and heavy axle loads.The technology has also recently been granted a patent. The low-density polyethylene (LDPE) used in the process — a soft, flexible and lightweight thermoplastic made from petroleum — includes discarded irrigation pipes, waste files and plastic folders. The material has been processed with the support of local recyclers and MSMEs, creating an opportunity to integrate local waste recycling with infrastructure development.“Laboratory evaluations have shown that LDPE-modified bitumen provides better resistance to moisture damage and greater resistance to rutting at high temperatures. The modified binder increases the stiffness and high-temperature performance of asphalt, helping pavements withstand permanent deformation under heavy traffic loads and extreme temperatures,” an official said.
Article Summary: India generates around 25,000 tonne of plastic waste every day. Pilot test section was laid on the main carriageway of NH-44 in Jhansi. Officials associated with the pilot said the technology has potential to reduce conventional bitumen consumption by around 4%.

NEW DELHI: Air India has suspended a pilot who was reportedly found tipsy when he was to operate a Zurich-Delhi flight earlier this month. The Zurich-Delhi flight of Sept 6 had to be rescheduled after the pilot was found unfit to operate the same and till alternate crew was arranged. With the airline having faced similar issues in the past few months, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has asked it to improve its checks and balances. The India regulator was apprised of the Zurich case by its Swiss counterpart."In the recent Zurich case involving a cockpit crew member, the individual was immediately removed from operating duties upon receipt of a preliminary breath analyser test report from local authorities and referred for further medical evaluation. The employee was subsequently repatriated to India as a passenger and remains under suspension pending the final medical examination report and completion of the investigation. Appropriate disciplinary action will be taken based on the findings," said an AI official.The airline, which recently terminated a pilot who had failed dope test after operating a badly rattled aircraft to Delhi, has seen multiple cases of tipsy pilots in the recent past.This Jan a pilot was detained at Vancouver airport after reeking of alcohol just before operating a flight to India.AI, whose safety practices are under the lens since last June Ahmedabad crash, says it "maintains an uncompromising commitment to safety, regulatory compliance and professional conduct across all aspects of its operations.""The airline follows a zero-tolerance policy towards any violation of safety, security or regulatory requirements. Any confirmed breach of established protocols is dealt with firmly, with disciplinary action taken in accordance with applicable regulations and company policies. This approach is consistent with Air India's longstanding policy that safety-related violations, particularly those involving alcohol, prohibited substances or conduct that could compromise operational safety, are treated with the utmost seriousness," the official added.Following the recent instances of crew failing dope and breath analyser (for alcohol) tests, AI says it has "has reinforced its expectations of professional conduct and regulatory compliance through multiple interventions across the organisation. A communication from the head of flight operations was issued to all pilots reiterating the airline's zero-tolerance policy towards the use of prohibited substances and reporting for duty under the influence of alcohol or drugs."The communication underscored the responsibilities associated with operating an aircraft and reaffirmed that there can be no compromise on safety, integrity or regulatory compliance.... Air India conducts regular awareness and compliance programmes for pilots and other employees (focussing on) regulatory obligations and licensing requirements; professional conduct standards; substance abuse regulations. ...."
Article Summary: The Zurich-Delhi flight of Sept 6 had to be rescheduled after the pilot was found unfit to operate the same and till alternate crew was arranged. The airline, which recently terminated a pilot who had failed dope test after operating a badly rattled aircraft, has seen multiple cases of tipsy pilots in the recent past.

NEW DELHI: EC, which is reeling under allegations of faultlines among its members, is now being questioned over a software update recently made in the application used by booth level officers, with its description on the Apple app store reading "mark VIP elector-related changes".EC sources told TOI Friday the instruction to BLOs on "flagging of marked electors" was a standard instruction, which was part of all three special intensive revision orders approved by the commission.The instruction to field officers to "mark" prominent electors in their jurisdictional areas has figured in EC's instructions for all special summary revisions, well before SIR was conceived, they said. For instance, Para 20 of the SSR exercise ordered by EC on May 29, 2023, with Jan 1, 2024, as the qualifying date, directed the "flagging of marked electors, viz MP/MLA/MLC, holders of declared offices and personalities from fields of arts, culture, journalism, sports, members of judiciary and public services, etc". Para 21 said the electoral registration officers were to ensure that the names were in the proposed draft roll.The same instruction was reiterated in the SIR order for Bihar dated June 24, 2025, and the orders for SIR Phase 2 and 3.Nowhere in the SIR or SSR instructions has the terminology 'VIP' been used. "It somehow made it to the app description," an officer said. EC officials said the BLO app software update was meant to help such prominent persons "marked" in the electoral database by flagging any notices served and enabling the proof furnished by them to be uploaded on the app without delay.Meanwhile, EC sources said the postponement of the electoral literacy club conferences in UP had nothing to do with the row and the decision was made on Sept 21.On reports alleging annual confidential reports were held up due to differences between commission members, EC officials said such delays were not unusual. TOI has further learnt there have been few full commission meetings in the past few months.
Article Summary: EC is reeling under allegations of faultlines among its members. Software update recently made in the application used by booth level officers. Its description on the Apple app store reading "mark VIP elector-related changes" EC sources said instruction to BLOs on "flagging of marked electors" was a standard instruction.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Friday asked BJP members to draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi to blend social reforms with their political work instead of focusing on vote bank politics."When we look at Mahatma Gandhi's life, we see he fought against the British and led the freedom movement. But he was also a great social reformer. He always worked against social evils. We as political workers too should not merely focus on vote-bank politics and allow things to continue as they are. We must continue working for social reforms," he said.He was interacting virtually with participants of "Seva Yatra", a motorcyle rally from Varanasi to Vadnagar organised by BJP to mark his 76th birthday and his continuous stint of 25 years as head of govt.Modi drew from his own experience as a frequent traveller across the length and breadth of India and said it has deeply enriched his life and values. "The message of service should be spread not merely by our words but action," he said, highlighting the felicitation of sanitation workers and other service-oriented programmes to make his point. Serving people is serving the country, he said, adding that BJP ideologue Deen Dayal Upadhyay, whose birth anniversary fell on Friday, put serving people at the core of his ideology.He praised those who carried out the cleanliness work in Prayagraj, noting that their efforts made the 'Kumbh Mela' famous worldwide for sanitation and elevated India's honour."So, I felt compelled to wash the feet of those who have enhanced India's honour so much, to seek their blessings," he said.Modi also said over the past 12 years, the gap between cities and villages in India has significantly narrowed and infrastructure in villages has improved to a great extent. He said self-reliance among women has also increased in the country.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi asks BJP members to blend social reforms with their political work. He was interacting virtually with participants of "Seva Yatra" to mark his 76th birthday. Modi drew from his own experience as a frequent traveller across the length of India.

Article Title: Amazon, Flipkart & JioMart fined for illegal herbicide sale
Article Text:
Representative image

Bharat NCAP 2.0, planned for October 2027, will look beyond what happens when a car crashes. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants, pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and what happens after an accident.Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari announced the proposed timeline at the SIAM Annual Convention in September. The second phase is being planned as the first phase of Bharat New Car Assessment Programme, or Bharat NCAP, approaches the end of its current cycle.According to the ministry of road transport and highways’ draft AIS-197 Revision 1, the first phase of Bharat NCAP began on October 1, 2023 and is valid until September 30, 2027. The draft revision has been prepared as the framework for Bharat NCAP 2.0.The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a car’s performance, not just in a crash, but before, during and after one.Bharat NCAP is India’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023.The programme applies to type-approved passenger vehicles in the M1 category with a gross vehicle weight of less than 3.5 tonnes. It is voluntary, which means manufacturers can offer eligible vehicles for assessment.The programme is anchored by the Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), while testing is carried out through designated agencies with the required infrastructure.At its core, Bharat NCAP gives car buyers a common safety benchmark. A vehicle must already meet mandatory regulatory requirements to be sold in India. Bharat NCAP goes a step further by putting eligible vehicles through specified tests and awarding them a rating of between one and five stars.The idea is fairly simple: instead of looking only at a car’s price, design or features, buyers get an additional reference point to understand how the vehicle performs in standardised safety tests.The government has also positioned the programme as a way to encourage manufacturers to improve vehicle safety and strengthen the safety standards of cars made in India.The existing programme broadly assesses three areas:Vehicles are subjected to prescribed crash tests and other assessments. Their performance across these parameters is then used to arrive at the overall star rating.The current framework includes a 64 kmph offset frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side movable deformable barrier test and a pole side impact test, among other checks prescribed under AIS-197.The assessment therefore goes beyond simply asking whether the passenger compartment remains intact.Adult Occupant Protection examines the risk of injury to adults in different crash conditions and seating positions. Child Occupant Protection looks at the protection offered to younger passengers, including the use and installation of child restraint systems.Safety Assist Technologies, meanwhile, covers technologies designed to help prevent crashes or reduce their severity.A car may offer different levels of protection to adults and children, so Bharat NCAP evaluates the two separately.The adult assessment focuses on occupant protection during prescribed crash scenarios, while the child assessment considers how effectively younger occupants are protected and how child restraint systems work within the vehicle.This also means that a car’s overall star rating is not simply a score from one crash test. It reflects performance across several safety parameters.For consumers, the individual scores can therefore provide more information than looking at the star rating alone.Bharat NCAP is anchored by CIRT, with testing carried out through designated testing agencies that have the required facilities.The wider automotive testing ecosystem includes agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT).Manufacturers submit eligible vehicles for assessment under the programme. The existing framework specifies procedures around the variant selected for testing, including provisions concerning the base variant of a model.That distinction matters when reading a Bharat NCAP result. A rating should not automatically be assumed to apply to every variant of a model unless the official assessment covers those variants.Bharat NCAP ratings range from one to five stars. A higher rating indicates stronger performance under the programme’s prescribed assessment criteria.But a five-star rating is not a guarantee that occupants will escape injury in every real-world crash. NCAP testing is conducted under standardised conditions and is intended to provide a basis for comparing vehicle safety performance.It is also important to distinguish Bharat NCAP from the mandatory certification requirements for selling a vehicle in India.Bharat NCAP is voluntary and is designed to provide consumers with additional information beyond the mandatory regulatory framework. A vehicle being tested or rated under Bharat NCAP should therefore not be confused with regulatory approval.Since its launch, Bharat NCAP has increasingly become part of the safety conversation around new car launches. The ratings have also become a factor in how manufacturers present their vehicles to consumers, particularly as safety becomes a more visible consideration in the passenger-vehicle market.This is where the proposed second phase takes a much wider approach.The draft AIS-197 Revision 1 divides Bharat NCAP 2.0 into five safety verticals:The change is significant because the current system focuses mainly on occupant protection and safety-assist technologies, while the proposed framework looks at the complete safety chain.The draft framework uses a 100-point assessment structure, with Crash Protection accounting for 55% of the assessment. The remaining weightage covers the other safety areas.In other words, the crash itself will still be a major part of the rating, but it will no longer be the only part of the safety story.Bharat NCAP 2.0 proposes expanding the Crash Protection assessment to five mandatory crash tests:Adult and child occupant protection will continue to be assessed separately.The addition of full-width frontal and rear-impact tests means the proposed system will examine crash scenarios beyond the core tests in the existing framework.That gives the second phase a wider testing footprint and allows different types of impacts to form part of the overall safety assessment.One of the biggest differences in Bharat NCAP 2.0 is that the programme is designed to look at what happens before a crash as well.Crash Avoidance is one of the five proposed verticals. It focuses on technologies and vehicle characteristics that can help prevent a collision or reduce its severity.Safe Driving is another proposed category, widening the assessment beyond the vehicle’s passive protection features.Together, these categories shift the focus from simply asking, “How well does this car perform when it crashes?” to a broader question: “How does this vehicle contribute to safety across different stages of a road incident?”Bharat NCAP 2.0 also proposes a separate Vulnerable Road User Protection category. This brings pedestrians and other vulnerable road users more directly into the safety assessment.Post-Crash Safety is one of the five proposed assessment areas. Minister Gadkari described Bharat NCAP 2.0 as covering the entire safety chain, including post-crash evacuation and care. “We are going to evaluate the entire crash chain,” Gadkari said, adding that new technologies developed globally as well as by startups would be considered under the programme.This means the assessment is intended to extend beyond the instant of impact and examine safety considerations in the period immediately after a crash.It adds another layer to the programme’s approach: avoiding the crash where possible, protecting people during the impact, and addressing safety after the collision.For buyers, Bharat NCAP offers an additional way to compare cars beyond mandatory safety requirements.A consumer can look at a vehicle’s overall rating as well as its adult and child protection performance and the safety technologies considered in the assessment.The rating is not meant to replace other factors involved in buying a car. Price, size, fuel efficiency, features, driving requirements and other considerations remain relevant, but the proposed 2.0 framework would expand that information further.Buyers could eventually have a broader picture of how a car performs across crash protection, crash avoidance, safe driving, vulnerable-road-user protection and post-crash safety.Bharat NCAP is one part of a much larger road-safety challenge, focusing on the structure of vehicles. Vehicle design and safety technology can influence the outcome of a crash, but they cannot address every reason why accidents happen.The ministry has identified several factors associated with road crashes, including speeding, mobile-phone use, drunken driving, wrong-side driving, lane indiscipline, jumping red lights and failure to use helmets and seat belts. Vehicle condition, road conditions and weather can also play a role.Government data recorded 1,68,491 road accident fatalities in 2022.Bharat NCAP therefore addresses one part of this wider equation: the safety performance of vehicles. Its proposed second phase would broaden that role by looking at what a vehicle can do to help avoid crashes, how it protects people when a crash occurs, how it protects vulnerable road users and what happens afterwards.The current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until September 30, 2027. The government has proposed introducing Bharat NCAP 2.0 from October 2027, with the draft AIS-197 Revision 1 serving as the framework for the next phase.The proposed transition would take India’s vehicle safety-rating system from a relatively focused crash and occupant-protection programme to a broader safety assessment.The familiar one-to-five-star rating would remain the consumer-facing language of vehicle safety, but the assessment behind it is set to become much more comprehensive.The bigger shift is in the question Bharat NCAP is trying to answer. Instead of looking only at how a car performs when it is involved in a crash, the proposed system would examine the vehicle’s safety journey from avoiding a collision to protecting occupants and vulnerable road users, and supporting safety after the crash.That could give Indian car buyers a wider set of safety information to consider when choosing their next vehicle.
Article Summary: Bharat NCAP is India’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023. The current framework includes a 64 kmph frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side side test and other checks. The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a car's performance.

Article Title: Indian Medical Parliamentarians’ Forum organises National Policy Summit on ‘Swasth bharat se saksham bharat’ to reimagine MedTech access in India
Article Text:
The Indian Medical Parliamentarians’ Forum (IMPF) convened the National Policy Summit on MedTech Access on September 22

Swasth Bharat Se Saksham Bharat

| Reimagining MedTech Access in India

.

‘Expanding access to quality care through MedTech innovation,’

“Innovation without access has limited impact, and access without evidence cannot be sustained. For India to build a globally competitive medical technology ecosystem, we need stronger indigenous research and development, credible clinical evidence, appropriate health technology assessment and sustainable reimbursement mechanisms.

Manufacturing must be supported by the right clinical skills, infrastructure and technical ecosystem.

Our ultimate objective must be Indian innovation, global-quality technology and affordable access for every patient who needs it.”

Manoj Kumar Joshi, Co-Chair and Secretary, Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers

Our regulatory system must evolve to ensure products developed in India meet globally credible standards. ”

Dr Prashant P. Joshi

“Medical institutions should not be limited to validating technologies developed elsewhere; they should identify unmet clinical needs and work with engineers, researchers and innovators to develop solutions.

Stronger collaboration between medical and engineering institutions through joint research, academic programmes, fellowships and training can significantly strengthen India’s medical technology ecosystem.

”

Dr Gaurav Shanker Pradhan

“Access to medical technology is not simply about making a device available. Meaningful impact is possible only when healthcare professionals can use it safely, confidently and effectively.

Dr Shailesh Kumar Yadav, IAS, Joint Director, National Health Authority

Dr Neha Dumka

Dr Shivaji Kalge

Article Title: Trai launches platform to rate buildings on digital connectivity
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: You will soon be able to check if receiving a mobile call will mean running to the balcony of your home in the hope of getting network coverage just as you do in your current residence. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India ( Trai ) Friday launched a platform that will rate buildings based on their digital connectivity, enabling people to choose accordingly.Trai Friday launched a "digital connectivity rating" (DCR) platform for the same and also a mobile app for testing digital connectivity. Which means like being rated on green parameters like water and power usage, buildings will have a new rating too that could mean avoiding homes where taking a call means standing in an open balcony.Trai chairman Anil Kumar Lahoti said: “The Digital Connectivity Rating Platform establishes a transparent and standardised framework for assessing the digital connectivity readiness of properties. By making ratings publicly searchable and verify the certificates, the platform will empower consumers with credible and comparable information. It will help them make more informed choices about homes and offices with strong and reliable connectivity, supporting smoother calls, downloads and access to online services.It will also enable consumers to recognise the value of digital connectivity infrastructure built into a property, while encouraging property managers to plan such infrastructure at the appropriate stage of property development.”The platform offers a public rating search page where consumers can search for a rated property by property name, or location. They can view the property’s digitally signed rating certificate and verify its authenticity through the QR code provided on the certificate. Based on this information consumer can make an informed choice while selecting the desired property prior to making the final purchase or lease decision."The platform provides a public interface for consumers to view the properties rated for digital connectivity. It brings property managers (PMs) registered Digital Connectivity Rating Agency (DCRA) and consumer onto a common digital interface. Property managers can register their properties in category of public, govt, commercial, private, submit rating applications, upload the prescribed information and documents, select a registered DCRA and track the status of their application through the platform. The platform supports the prescribed assessment workflow for both constructed and under-construction properties," Trai said in a statement .The platform enables the digital workflow relating to assessment, report generation, certification and publication of ratings. Consumers and other stakeholders will be able to search rated properties, view published ratings, verify the corresponding certificates and compare the properties of interest." Field assessments will be facilitated through a dedicated DCRA mobile app. The app will enable authorised DCRA to undertake in-building digital connectivity measurements in accordance with the prescribed testing methodology. Property information received through the web portal and the assessment data captured through the mobile application will be synchronised in the platform," said the statement .The DCR framework provides a standardised method for evaluating digital connectivity within properties. The assessment considers prescribed parameters relating to fibre readiness, mobile network availability, in-building solutions and Wi-Fi infrastructure, with applicable benchmarks for different categories of properties." The framework seeks to encourage the consideration of Digital Connectivity Infrastructure at appropriate stages of property development and facilitate the assessment of infrastructure and connectivity performance in existing properties. The Digital Connectivity Rating (DCR) Platform can be accessed at: https://dcrp.trai.gov.in ," it added.
Article Summary: Trai Friday launched a "digital connectivity rating" (DCR) platform for the same and also a mobile app for testing digital connectivity. Trai chairman Anil Kumar Lahoti: “The Digital Connectivity Rating Platform establishes a transparent and standardised framework for assessing the digital connectivity readiness of properties"

Article Title: After split verdict, SC refers law on EC appointment to larger bench; decision comes amid row over EC functioning
Article Text:
SC: Constitution bench should deal with case to prevent delay

SC: Constitution bench should deal with case to prevent delay

Poll Vote & Share your view How important is it for the Supreme Court to resolve the appointment of election commissioners issue quickly? Very important Somewhat important Not important at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: On a day when Election Commission found itself under the scanner, a two-judge bench of Supreme Court gave a split verdict on whether the issue of validity of the law on appointment of CEC/ECs be referred to a constitution bench, but later agreed to refer the case to a larger bench for the sake of early adjudication of the contentious issue.Validity of several provisions of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 has been challenged on the ground that the law gives the executive "overwhelming" power to appoint its nominee as election commissioner, as the selection panel composed of the PM, a Cabinet minister and the leader of the opposition is designed to give govt a 2:1 majority. The petitioners contended that EC's independence would be compromised in this process.The 2023 law was framed to replace an SC verdict which had directed that selection be done by a committee of the PM, CJI and leader of the opposition until Parliament determined the composition by passing a law. "Speaking in one voice would have better served institutional cohesion. Unfortunately, the court is divided in its opinion," a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and S C Sharma said.The hearing in the case went on for five days and at the fag end of proceedings, the Centre had sought referral of the case to a constitution bench.Noting that appointment of CEC/ECs was being litigated for last 11 years in SC after a petition was filed in 2015, the bench decided that the case should not be referred to a three-judge bench, which is the normal procedure, but to a constitution bench to settle the issue once and for all. It reasoned that a decision by a three-judge bench would be of little worth and only delay adjudication of the significant issue(s) that these writ petitions raise."Thus, we direct that the papers be placed before the CJI for considering the desirability of constituting a constitution bench of such number of judges to decide the question of vires of Sec 7 and the other provisions of Act," the bench said.The bench expressed hope that the case would be given priority as the issues raised were of "foundational importance to the democratic fabric of the country and its citizenry"."Petitioners seem to be justified in expressing their anxiety that references to five-judge benches remain unresolved for years. If statistics are any guide, none can say with any reasonable degree of certainty when long-pending references will get resolved. Undisputedly, this is an area of grave concern and the inordinate delay in resolution of the references is itself a source of institutional embarrassment which all stakeholders ought to strive to avoid. Self-introspection, indeed, is required," it said."We, thus, take this opportunity of requesting the Chief Justice to also explore the necessity of constituting a permanent five-judge bench to decide pure constitutional issues. This is not something novel that we are saying. It has been opined time and again by responsible citizens and we simply endorse their opinion. Given that resolving constitutional issues is the primary task of judges of this court, that must remain its core priority.Pendency of references for far too long, any period between five and 20 years or more, does not reflect well on the institution. It is time that the institution addresses the issue with the urgency and promptitude it deserves," the bench said.
Article Summary: Two-judge bench of Supreme Court gave a split verdict on whether the issue of validity of the law on appointment of CEC/ECs be referred to a constitution bench. The bench later agreed to refer the case to a larger bench for the sake of early adjudication of the contentious issue.

Article Title: SIR queries raised, but pertained to draft stage; focusing on some notes while ignoring others gives only one part of picture: EC
Article Text:
Dr. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, Gyanesh Kumar, Dr. Vivek Joshi

Focusing on some notes while ignoring others gives only one part of picture: EC

_

NEW DELHI: Faced with criticism for election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi being cut out of crucial decisions, the Election Commission on Wednesday said the “operational queries, inputs and suggestions” raised over the past 10 months by the two commissioners, including on the special intensive revision (SIR) process, remained limited to the draft stages and were part of the standard administrative practice and decision-making process at the Commission.All decisions taken by the commission in the past one year, including SIR, “are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full commission,” EC asserted in a statement rebutting the contention that the chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar was acting unilaterally.EC was reacting to a report in Indian Express claiming that the two election commissioners had objected to steps taken by the poll panel on 14 occasions over 10 months, including the changes made to Form 6 as part of SIR, restricting field officers’ access to electoral roll databases and even regarding postings and foreign tours involving EC personnel.Sandhu and Joshi even wrote to the Cabinet secretary separately on July 29, complaining about redistribution of work by the senior deputy election commissioner (DEC) in charge of administration EC and the resultant centralisation of decision -making , said the report.In its statement, EC said that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution before a final decision is taken.“Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks and balances are standard, ongoing practices to ensure transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour." EC said all its actions as well as official orders, decisions and administrative decisions have been in accordance with laws and commission's instructions and carry full legal sanction."Highlighting certain specific internal notes/observations spread over the period of 10 months while overlooking the much larger body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives give only one part of the picture," EC said adding that its decisions, instructions, 40 new initiatives and conduct of polls in six states/UTs in the past one year were all based on unanimous decisions by the commission in the past one year.Sources in EC said the objections were largely raised in written notes sent by the election commissioners to the deputy election commissioners (DECs), in many cases after they had signed on the concerned file following a unanimous decision; including in the cases of changes made to Form 6. The two commissioners, Joshi in May and Sandhu in August, had argued that changes in Form 6 could be carried out only by the government. However, sources maintained, after they along with the CEC unanimously approved the file relating to SIR orders for Bihar (Phase 1) and then a dozen states (Phase 2), which listed the revised Form 6 and the accompanying declaration on citizenship. In fact, by the time Sandhu objected, the Supreme Court had already upheld the validity of SIR as well as the processes followed by EC, sources said.As part of his case against powers getting centralised and CEC not taking his two colleagues in confidence, Sandhu had raised the issue of who had authorised filing of appeals on EC's behalf before the SIR tribunals in West Bengal. Sources, however, told TOI that this was as per the Supreme Court order dated April 1, 2026, particularly para 9 that stated that appeals may be filed by "persons whose names have been excluded from the voters list" or "by the authorities of the ECI, who may be aggrieved by the inclusion of names by the adjudicatory authorities".On the commissioners’ alleged objection to centralisation of the electoral roll database or ERONet/ECINet, allegedly with restricted access to field officers like the electoral registration officers (EROs) to decide on addition of deletion of names, the Commission said digital platforms such as ECINet operate under strict data security protocols to prevent unauthorised tampering, manipulation, etc. "IT security checks and audit controls are standard cybersecurity measures implemented across national databases. Statutory authorities, including EROs and district election officers (DEOs), function as per statutory powers for registration and deletion under law,” said EC. Sources in EC told TOI that while EROs and DEOs may have faced access issues due to system errors on some occasions, they have full access to electors databases and have been deciding on roll updations during SIR.Sources in the Commission did not contest Joshi's claim that agenda and minutes of EC meetings were not being circulated, but said this has been the norm before the present commission assumed office.Responding to the objections to decision of the DEC (Administration) to change the officer in charge of IT division, sources said that powers to decide appointment, recruitment, transfers and postings of officers above the level of section officer and posting and transfer of personal staff of election commissioners and DECs were delegated to DEC (Administration) in 1997.Regarding Joshi's April 16 objection to EC officers being sent on foreign trips without the "commission's" approval, sources said the power in this regard has been with the CEC since long.Reacting to Sandhu's objection that he had learnt of EC's new IT modules, portals etc from the media, sources pointed that both Sandhu and Joshi were present at ECINet's launch on January 22.
Article Summary: Election Commission says objections raised over past 10 months were limited to draft stages. All decisions taken by the commission in the past one year, including SIR, “are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full commission,” EC says.

Article Title: Penn’s Cave and Wildlife Park seeks new owner for first time since 1908, with historic 1,400-acre Pennsylvania property listed at an asking price of $34 million
Article Text:
Penn’s Cave and Wildlife Park is seeking a new owner for the first time in 118 years. (Photo: Bright MLS)

Historic cave draws visitors from around the world

Penn’s Cave includes a roughly quarter-mile natural limestone cavern and guided boat tours. (Photo: Penn's Cave)

Wildlife park features native and exotic species

The 1,400-acre property is home to bison, elk, wolves, mountain lions and other wildlife. (Photo: Bright MLS)

Potential state park deal had been considered

The Campbell family says preserving Penn’s Cave’s legacy will remain a priority during the sale. (Photo: Bright MLS)

Antique machinery show’s future also uncertain

Penn’s Cave and Wildlife Park in Pennsylvania is seeking a new owner for the first time in 118 years, with the 1,400-acre property listed at an asking price of $34 million. The Campbell family, which has owned and operated the Centre County attraction since 1908, announced Wednesday that it will begin accepting proposals from potential buyers on October 1.The property includes Penn’s Cave, described as the only all-water cavern and wildlife park in the United States. Owners Russ and Jeanne Schleiden said the decision to seek a buyer was not taken lightly, stressing that maintaining the attraction and its natural resources remains a priority during the transition.“Penn’s Cave has been our family’s legacy. We have a lot of pride in this property and the business,” the owners said in a written statement quoted by the Centre Daily Times. They added that the family would continue maintaining the property with the same level of commitment while searching for its next owner.“Continuing the experience we’re known for is our greatest priority throughout this transition,” they said.Estimated to be about 30 million years old, Penn’s Cave is a roughly quarter-mile-long natural limestone cave featuring guided boat tours. It is the only cave in Pennsylvania listed on the National Register of Historic Places.A nomination form dating to 1883 described the cave’s formations as “varied and fantastic to an extraordinary degree” and called it a “picturesquely beautiful spectacle.” The document also described Penn’s Cave and its boat tours as the most widely known tourist attraction in Centre County and among the most popular attractions in Pennsylvania.The business says millions of people from around the world have visited Penn’s Cave during its nearly 150-year history.According to a company press release, four generations of the Campbell family have worked to preserve the property, establish water rights and acquire surrounding land to support the continued stewardship of its natural resources. The property generates as much as 11 million gallons of water each day.Beyond the cave, the property includes a wildlife park that is home to a range of animals, including bison, Texas longhorns, elk, white-tailed deer, wild horses, donkeys, mountain lions and wolves.Other attractions include a maze, gemstone panning, picnic grounds and off-road mountain tours. The property also has a private airport that allows pilots and their passengers to arrive directly at the attraction.The family said finding a new owner who understands the property’s potential and is committed to its long-term stewardship will be central to the sale process.“Preserving the business and finding the next steward of the land who can see the immense potential of the property and continue the legacy” are among the family’s priorities.The sale announcement comes roughly two months after the family revealed that it was considering selling the property to Pennsylvania’s Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.The proposal would have turned Penn’s Cave into Pennsylvania’s 126th state park and received support from Centre County commissioners and state Rep. Kerry Benninghoff. However, the state budget was passed without legislation that would have facilitated the transfer.During a July commissioners meeting, Benninghoff said several investors had expressed interest in purchasing the property and dividing it into multiple parcels for development. He described that possibility as “a real shame.”It remains unclear whether Gov. Josh Shapiro’s administration continues to have an interest in acquiring the property. Benninghoff has said he would introduce legislation for the transfer again if he is reelected.The possible sale has also raised questions about the future of the Nittany Antique Machinery Association’s events at Penn’s Cave. The organization’s shows are billed as the largest antique machinery shows on the East Coast, with the annual event dating back to 1975.The association has been seeking a five-year lease renewal. Penn’s Cave, however, sought a one-year lease with new conditions, according to court documents.In a letter included in a court filing, Penn’s Cave said its plans for the property were a “strong consideration” in its lease negotiations. The existing lease expires on December 31.The association withdrew its request for judicial intervention on Monday, saying it hopes the move will create an opportunity for constructive negotiations between the two organizations.“We respect Penn’s Cave and understand that it has interests and decisions to make regarding its property,” association President Doug Leitch said in a written statement. “Our hope is that both sides can put those interests on the table, listen to one another and find common ground.”Proposals for the 1,400-acre Penn’s Cave and Wildlife Park will be accepted beginning October 1, as the Campbell family begins the process of determining who will take over the historic Pennsylvania attraction.
Article Summary: Penn’s Cave and Wildlife Park in Pennsylvania is seeking a new owner for the first time in 118 years. The 1,400-acre property is home to bison, elk, wolves, mountain lions and other wildlife. The Campbell family, which has owned and operated the Centre County attraction since 1908, will begin accepting proposals from potential buyers on October 1.

Article Title: From a $1.75 million school gift to a $3 million hospital donation: How Russell Wilson and Ciara built a foundation around helping children
Article Text:
From a $1.75 million school gift to a $3 million hospital donation: How Russell Wilson and Ciara built a foundation around helping children

How Russell Wilson and Ciara built the Why Not You Foundation around children

From a Seattle school to major gifts for children’s health and hunger

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Russell Wilson and Ciara, the words “Why not you?” have become closely tied to the work they do for children and families. Through the Why Not You Foundation, which they started in 2014, the couple has supported education, children’s health and efforts to fight hunger. The foundation said in 2023 that its partnerships had helped raise more than $13 million for these causes. Since then, its work has continued with several large donations and community programs.The idea behind the foundation came from a message Wilson learned from his father, Harrison Wilson III, who encouraged him to believe that he could achieve his goals even when others doubted him. Wilson later carried that message into his charity work, with the foundation focusing on giving young people better access to education, health care and basic support.Wilson had already been spending time with children at Seattle Children’s Hospital before the foundation was created. His visits became a regular part of his life, and his connection with young patients later became an important part of the foundation’s work. The foundation has also supported pediatric cancer research and programs aimed at helping families facing food insecurity.Education has been another major part of their work. In 2020, the Why Not You Foundation committed about $1.75 million to help rebrand and support Cascade Midway Academy, a charter school south of Seattle.The school later became Why Not You Academy and opened to high school students, with a focus on personalized learning, mentorship and work-based opportunities.The couple has also taken their work into communities where they have lived and worked. In 2023, through a partnership with CommonSpirit Health, the foundation helped provide $1 million in grants to 10 organizations in Colorado and Utah. Each group received $100,000 for work involving areas such as education, health equity, food security and support for children and young people.The foundation’s more recent donations show that its work has expanded beyond education. In November 2025, the Why Not You Foundation announced a $3 million gift to Mount Sinai Kravis Children’s Hospital in New York. The money is supporting two therapeutic spaces, including a Child Life Zone Theater and a play space for children receiving cancer and blood disease care.Just a month later, the foundation announced another $500,000 donation to the Atlanta Community Food Bank and ATL Cares. According to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution, the money was expected to help provide more than one million meals to families dealing with food insecurity.In February 2026, the foundation announced a $2 million donation to the Los Cabos Children’s Foundation in Mexico. The gift is being used to expand health and rehabilitation services for children and families in Baja California Sur.Their fundraising efforts have also reached large numbers. In 2025, the Youth Athlete of the Year competition raised $21.66 million, with the money set to support both the Why Not You Foundation and the V Foundation for Cancer Research.The foundation now also runs Why Not You Centers, which are designed to give young people access to mentorship, academic support, creative programs and other resources. According to the foundation, centers are open in Pittsburgh, Atlanta and Pasadena, with more locations planned for 2026.
Article Summary: Russell Wilson and Ciara started the Why Not You Foundation in 2014. The foundation has supported education, children’s health and efforts to fight hunger. In 2020, the foundation committed about $1.75 million to help rebrand and support Cascade Midway Academy.

Article Title: A Michigan family lost a home assessed at $194,400 over a disputed $2,242 property-tax bill; the county sold it for $76,008, the buyer resold it for $195,000, and the Supreme Court vacated the lower r
Article Text:
Dispute over a primary residence tax rate

Foreclosure and dramatic resale values

Lower courts divide over fair compensation

Supreme Court sets constitutional baseline

Concurring opinions highlight auction fairness

The United States Supreme Court ruled that a Michigan family whose $194,400 home was sold at a public auction over a $2,242 tax debt is entitled to receive only the surplus cash from the sale, not the home's full open-market value. The judgment in Pung v. Isabella County sets a nationwide legal standard for measuring compensation after a fairly conducted tax sale. Writing for the majority, Justice Samuel Alito said that when local authorities seize and sell a home for unpaid property taxes, “just compensation” under the Fifth Amendment is based on the actual public auction price, not a hypothetical market value. The Court issued its decision on June 23, 2026, vacated the Sixth Circuit's judgment, and sent the case back for further proceedings.The legal fight began in Union Township, Isabella County, Michigan. Scott Pung bought the three-bedroom ranch-style home in 1991 for $125,000. The home was the family's primary residence. After Scott Pung died in 2004, his wife, Donnamarie, continued living there. After Donnamarie died in 2008, their son Marc and his family continued to live in the house. The property remained owned by Scott Pung's estate, with Donnamarie and Marc as beneficiaries.In 2010, the local tax assessor removed the family's primary residence exemption. The assessor believed the family had failed to file an updated affidavit showing that the house was still their main home. She therefore taxed it as a second home for tax years 2007 through 2011. The family challenged the decision before the Michigan Tax Tribunal and won. The tribunal ruled that they did not owe the additional taxes charged to second homes. Instead, they owed the ordinary tax rate that applied to a primary residence. Even after that ruling, however, the family faced a real-property tax balance of $2,241.93.Because of the outstanding $2,241.93 tax bill, Isabella County officials began tax foreclosure proceedings. A Michigan trial court initially blocked the foreclosure, but the Michigan Court of Appeals later allowed it to continue. The county followed the procedures required by the Michigan General Property Tax Act, including a period in which the family could redeem the property, public notice of the sale, and a court judgment of foreclosure. The county then put the ranch home up for public auction. Tax records valued the property at $194,400. Despite that assessment, the highest bidder bought the home for $76,008 at the public tax sale. The investor who bought the home later sold it on the open market for $195,000, nearly the same as its earlier assessed value. The resale happened less than 18 months after the county auction. Meanwhile, Isabella County initially kept all of the auction proceeds.Michael Pung, acting as the personal representative of the estate of Timothy Scott Pung, sued Isabella County in federal court. He argued that keeping the property's value violated the Takings Clause of the Fifth Amendment and the Excessive Fines Clause of the Eighth Amendment. The federal District Court granted Pung partial summary judgment on his Fifth Amendment claim. The court ruled that the county had to return the surplus from the tax sale. But it rejected Pung's argument that he should receive compensation based on the home's full fair market value. Pung appealed to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit. The Sixth Circuit affirmed the decision. It ruled that when a municipality sells foreclosed property through a properly conducted public auction, the former owner is entitled to the amount received above the tax debt, and no more. That meant Pung was entitled to $73,766.07, the difference between the $76,008 sale price and the $2,241.93 tax debt.Pung asked the U.S. Supreme Court to decide whether compensation should instead be based on the home's full market value when a tax auction produces a much lower price. The Supreme Court agreed to hear the case and issued its decision on June 23, 2026. The justices held that the auction price is the constitutional starting point for measuring compensation after a tax sale, as long as the sale is fairly conducted in light of the country's history of tax sales. The Court rejected the idea that the government must pay the property's hypothetical open-market value. In the opinion, Justice Alito explained that using hypothetical market values could place heavy financial demands on local governments. He wrote: “Pung's fair-market-value theory would impose unprecedented burdens on jurisdictions that wish to collect unpaid taxes and might well make tax sales impractical.” The Court also pointed to a long history of tax sales in English and American law. It said governments have used property sales to collect unpaid taxes for centuries, while requiring them to return any money left after the tax debt and related costs were paid. The Court concluded that the proper constitutional baseline is the actual tax-sale price, not the home's hypothetical fair market value. It also ruled that the Eighth Amendment's Excessive Fines Clause does not require the government to return more than the surplus proceeds from a fairly conducted tax sale.Justice Sonia Sotomayor, joined by Justice Neil Gorsuch and Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, filed a separate opinion agreeing with the Court's judgment. She stressed that the decision does not define every requirement for a fair tax auction. “I do not read the Court's opinion as identifying the contours of a fair auction,” Justice Sotomayor wrote. She said the Court was leaving those questions for the lower courts if they were properly preserved in the case. The Supreme Court's decision vacated the Sixth Circuit's judgment and sent docket 25-95 back for further proceedings. The family is entitled to the $73,766.07 surplus from the county's $76,008 public auction, rather than compensation based on the home's $194,400 assessed value. The Sixth Circuit may also consider arguments about whether the county's foreclosure and sale procedures were fair, if those arguments were properly preserved.
Article Summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that a Michigan family whose $194,400 home was sold at a public auction over a $2,242 tax debt is entitled to receive only the surplus cash from the sale. Justice Samuel Alito said that when local authorities seize and sell a home for unpaid property taxes, “just compensation” under the Fifth Amendment is based on the actual public auction price, not a hypothetical market value.

Why ITAT Mumbai ruled in taxpayer’s favour

Lessons for employees

Your employer cuts Tax Deducted At source or TDS from your salary, but doesn’t deposit it. You get a tax demand notice. What do you do?A Mumbai-based IT professional faced this very situation when she received a tax demand of Rs 3.36 lakh, even though she had claimed Rs 3.91 lakh as TDS credit in her income tax return (ITR).For Assessment Year 2019-20, the woman reported an income of Rs 18.41 lakh in her ITR and claimed credit for Rs 3.91 lakh in TDS. However, she was given credit for only Rs 79,030, resulting in a tax demand of Rs 3.36 lakh.The reason was that her employer, an IT services company, had deducted TDS from her salary but had not deposited the amount with the government.She approached the Centralised Processing Centre (CPC) for rectification on several occasions, but her efforts did not resolve the issue.She subsequently filed a first appeal, which was rejected on the ground that it was time-barred. She then challenged the matter before the income tax appellate tribunal (ITAT), where she eventually got relief.The ITAT Mumbai observed that the woman had not received credit for the entire TDS amount because her employer had deducted tax from her salary but failed to remit it to the revenue.As the deducted amount was not deposited, the complete TDS credit did not appear in her Form 26AS.This led to the denial of her Rs 3.91 lakh TDS claim.She, however, produced several documents to establish that the tax had actually been deducted from her salary by her employer. These included her salary slips, Form 16, bank statements and other supporting records.After considering the documents and referring to recent rulings of the Supreme Court and a High Court, the tribunal held that an employee cannot be made liable for a tax demand where the employer has deducted tax at source from the employee’s salary income but failed to deposit the deducted amount with the government.The Rs 3.36 lakh tax demand will therefore also be nullified once the Assessing Officer verifies her claim of Rs 3.91 lakh in TDS and grants her the full credit, according to an ET report.In this case, the taxpayer succeeded because she was able to establish that TDS had actually been deducted from her salary.A taxpayer who can demonstrate that TDS was deducted, using documents such as Form 16 and salary slips, can rely on Section 205 of the Income Tax Act, 1961. In such a case, the Department cannot seek to recover the same tax from the employee.Once the TDS credit is allowed, the Rs 3.36 lakh tax demand will effectively stand nullified.Raghav Bajaj, Partner, Khaitan & Co says that the ITAT Mumbai ruling reinforces an important safeguard: where salary tax has demonstrably been withheld by an employer, the taxpayer employee should not bear the consequences of the employer’s failure to remit it.Section 205 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (corresponding to section 401 of Income-tax Act, 2025) draws a bright line: once tax is deducted, the obligation to remit it falls on the deductor, not the deductee.“By directing verification and grant of credit, the Tribunal recognises the evidentiary value of Form 16, salary records and banking trails. For taxpayers and practitioners, the implications are both reassuring and instructive,” he tells TOI.On the dispute resolution front, this decision makes clear that automated CPC processing under Section 143(1) - which matches TDS claims against Form 26AS - cannot be the final word where genuine deductions have occurred.“A mismatch in Form 26AS, standing alone, does not extinguish a legitimate TDS credit,” he says.According to Kuldip Kumar, Partner at Mainstay Tax Advisors LLP, the decision of the Mumbai ITAT is a useful reiteration of an important principle relating to TDS credit.There have been several other judgments of different Benches of the ITAT and various High Courts that have favoured the assessee in this regard.“The legal position is now strongly supported by a consistent line of judicial decisions that, where tax has actually been deducted at source but has not been deposited by the deductor, the assessee should not be denied the corresponding TDS credit or be made liable to pay the same tax again, provided the assessee is able to establish that the tax was in fact deducted,” Kumar tells TOI.Importantly, Kumar notes that this principle is not confined to tax deducted from salary. It can also apply to TDS deducted from other domestic payments, including contractor or professional fees, rent, interest, dividend and similar payments.In relation to their financial affairs, it is important for taxpayers to maintain proper documentation to establish that TDS was actually deducted.According to Kumar, for salaried taxpayers, this could include salary slips, employment letters and bank statements evidencing receipt of the net salary. In the case of other payments, copies of invoices, contracts or agreements, payment advice, ledger accounts and bank statements showing receipt of the net amount could serve as supporting evidence.It is also advisable to review Form 26AS/AIS periodically and reconcile the TDS reflected therein with the TDS actually deducted. Where a deduction is not reflected, the taxpayer should, where possible, promptly write to the employer or payer and request confirmation and correction. Such contemporaneous correspondence can also become important corroborative evidence if the deductor subsequently fails to deposit the TDS or file the relevant TDS statement.“Given the increasing reliance on electronic processing, a TDS mismatch may result in an automated demand being raised when the TDS claimed in the return is not reflected in Form 26AS/AIS. In such circumstances, the taxpayer should promptly seek rectification with the CPC / jurisdictional Assessing Officer with appropriate documentary evidence and seek grant of the TDS credit and consequential rectification of the demand,” Kuldip Kumar says.
Article Summary: Mumbai-based IT professional received a tax demand of Rs 3.36 lakh. She had claimed Rs 3,91 lakh as TDS credit in her income tax return (ITR) However, she was given credit for only Rs 79,030. The reason was that her employer had deducted TDS from her salary but had not deposited the amount with the government.

Article Title: KSI vs N3on net worth comparison: Which streamer is richer in 2026, inside their businesses, careers and more
