KSI (via Getty Images)

KSI vs N3on net worth comparison in 2026

Creator Estimated Net Worth Main Income Sources KSI $150 million YouTube, music, boxing, Prime, Sidemen, businesses, TV N3on $5 million Kick, YouTube, sponsorships, clips, promotions, merchandise

KSI launched the company with Logan Paul in 2022. A federal court order confirmed that KSI and Logan each own 20% of Prime.However, that percentage does not automatically reveal the value of KSI’s stake.Prime experienced enormous growth during its viral boom. Its sales later slowed. The company’s UK subsidiary reported turnover of £32.8 ($43.4) million in 2024, down from £112.2 million ($148.6m) in 2023. As a result, putting a precise value on KSI’s Prime holding would be speculative.KSI has also earned money from the Sidemen. The group developed businesses including clothing, restaurants, subscriptions, trading cards and other entertainment ventures. KSI also helped launch Misfits Boxing and has built a successful music career.His boxing career added another major source of income. KSI fought Joe Weller and Logan Paul before returning to the ring in 2022. He later fought Tommy Fury in 2023. In 2026, KSI said he was taking a break from boxing.N3on’s fortune has been built differently. Livestreaming is at the centre of his business. He became particularly prominent on Kick after moving away from traditional gaming content and focusing heavily on IRL streams.N3on has said that he can earn thousands of dollars per hour through Kick’s partner programme, depending on his audience and engagement. He also earns through sponsorships, promotional deals, YouTube and his extensive clipping network.His clipping operation has become a notable part of his business. Business Insider reported that N3on paid more than $1.4 million to 303 clippers during one five-week period. He has also said his wider clipping network includes around 1,000 people.KSI and N3on therefore represent two different models of internet wealth. KSI’s fortune has been built across entertainment, sports, consumer brands and investments. N3on’s earnings are more closely tied to livestreaming, viral content and digital partnerships.Their net-worth estimates are also likely to change. As their businesses and online careers develop.
Article Summary: KSI built his career through YouTube gaming, music, boxing, and the Sidemen. N3on rose through gaming videos, livestreams, viral clips, and IRL content. Both creators have turned their online popularity into businesses that go well beyond traditional YouTube videos.

Article Title: Delhi SIR: Colleges, universities to host special voter enrolment camps for young voters on Sep 29-30
Article Text:
The chief electoral officer of Delhi is organizing special camps for voter registration on September 29 and 30 (Representative image)





NEW DELHI: The Office of the chief electoral officer (CEO), Delhi, has directed all district election officers to organise special camps at colleges, universities and other educational institutions across the national capital on September 29 and 30 as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2026.The camps will be held from 9am to 3pm on both days and will focus on maximising enrolment of young voters aged 18 to 25, news agency ANI reported.Eligible students will be encouraged to fill Form-6 for inclusion in the electoral rolls.In a letter dated September 25, deputy chief electoral officer (ER) Prashant Kumar Prasad directed all DEOs to make necessary arrangements for the camps and ensure adequate electoral rolls, Form-6 applications and other required materials are available.The CEO office also directed officials to deploy non-teaching BLOs at the camps and asked principals and heads of educational institutions to disseminate information about the camps in advance and motivate eligible students to enrol.Applications received from students seeking enrolment in another district or Assembly Constituency will be forwarded to the concerned EROs/AEROs, according to the directions, ANI reported.Officials have also been asked to maintain proper records of all forms received at colleges and institutions, publicise the camps through social media and ensure regular monitoring at the district and Assembly Constituency levels.The camps are being organised during the claims and objections period of the SIR 2026.The CEO Delhi website says eligible electors whose names are not included in the draft electoral roll can apply for inclusion through Form-6 during the claims and objections period, which runs until September 30.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Chief electoral officer of Delhi is organizing special camps for voter registration on September 29 and 30. The camps will be held from 9am to 3pm on both days and will focus on maximising enrolment of young voters aged 18 to 25.Eligible students will be encouraged to fill Form-6 for inclusion in electoral rolls.

Article Title: Satya Niketan collapse: Delhi govt forms high-powered panel to examine student accommodation, frame PG rules
Article Text:
A committee has been established by the Delhi govt to assess student accommodation safety following the collapse of a building in Satya Niketan





NEW DELHI: The Delhi government has constituted a high-powered committee to examine student accommodation and safety in the capital and recommend time-bound measures, the Delhi high court was informed on Friday during a hearing on the September 6 Satya Niketan building collapse.The committee has already decided to prepare a regulatory framework for paying guest (PG) accommodation and private student hostels in Delhi.The submission was made during the hearing of a matter concerning the building collapse in Satya Niketan, where a boys' paying-guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus had collapsed while repair work was underway, killing seven people, including five students, and injuring several others.A bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia was informed by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) that immediately after the September 6 incident, the matter was taken up at the highest executive level of the civic body.The MCD also informed the court that five officers across the entire supervisory chain of the corporation, including a deputy commissioner, had been suspended.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Delhi government, MCD and Delhi Police, gave details of other steps taken by the authorities.The court also termed Delhi University's affidavit "absolutely vague". The varsity's counsel assured the court that a better response would be filed.According to the MCD's affidavit, the Delhi government constituted a magisterial inquiry into the collapse to examine issues including the validity of permissions, compliance with building bye-laws and the role of the concerned officials.The MCD said no sanctioned building plan had been approved for the property and that it had not been constructed pursuant to valid MCD permission.The civic body also said a time-bound survey and inspection of PG buildings identified across all 12 zones under its jurisdiction had been undertaken.Of 2,453 PG buildings surveyed, 2,342 were found to be visibly safe, 91 required minor repairs, 30 required major repairs and four were found to be in dangerous condition."In addition to that, eight load-bearing structures above ground-plus three storeys and 77 framed structures above ground-plus four storeys are being separately identified for close monitoring as the same may be vulnerable," it said.Cases involving any prima facie issue concerning immediate structural safety or danger to life are being prioritised for appropriate inspection and strict action in accordance with law, the MCD said in its affidavit.The Delhi government's High-Powered Committee on student accommodation and safety was constituted through a September 10 order to examine issues relating to student accommodation and safety in Delhi and recommend appropriate, time-bound measures."In its meeting held on September 15, the committee, among other decisions, resolved to prepare a regulatory framework for paying guest accommodations and private student hostels.It was decided that the Department of Training and Technical Education (DTTE) and the Department of Higher Education (DHE) shall jointly prepare a regulatory framework for PG accommodation and private student hostels," it said.The committee also decided that the framework would be developed in consultation with the stakeholder agency or department and should take into account the experience of other states and Union Territories in regulating PG accommodations.The Delhi Police, in its reply, said six accused, including the owners of the collapsed Satya Niketan building, had failed to take adequate safety precautions during construction or repair work, creating a situation that endangered human lives and ultimately caused deaths.It said the building collapsed due to excessive structural load or weakening of the existing structure, endangering human life and resulting in casualties.The MCD affidavit was filed in a pending PIL by law student Aniket Kumar Gupta, seeking urgent medical care and rehabilitation of affected students, Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of the deceased and preservation of crucial evidence relating to the collapse.The court permitted retired IPS officer Kiran Bedi to address it in the matter and asked the parties to also supply her with the documents they would place on record.The court listed the matter for further hearing on October 14 and said that if the Delhi government's High-Powered Committee meeting takes place in the meantime, its minutes should be placed on record.On September 7, the high court had ordered a high-level MCD inquiry into the building collapse and made it clear that the government could not evade responsibility.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: The committee has already decided to prepare a regulatory framework for paying guest (PG) accommodation and private student hostels in Delhi. The submission was made during the hearing of a matter concerning the building collapse in Satya Niketan. A boys' paying-guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus had collapsed.

Article Title: Intel cuts VP ranks from 450 to 200, CFO David Zinsner calls it a 'cultural problem'; says it contributed to products going through four or five...
Article Text:
Intel's leadership was hearing a different story from the one on the ground

Intel says 18A yields and 14A progress show the overhaul is working

Intel has cut the number of vice presidents at the company from about 450 at its peak to roughly 200. It has also halved its management layers from 12 to six as CEO Lip-Bu Tan tries to get the chipmaker to decide faster and ship on time. CFO David Zinsner shared the numbers at the Deutsche Bank Technology Conference, describing the old structure as a cultural problem that hurt Intel's execution for more than a decade.Zinsner said too many people across the organisation held veto power, so decisions kept stalling. The damage showed up in products. Chips often needed four or five development cycles before they were ready, when they should have reached production after the first attempt. Looking back at the last decade, he said much of Intel's trouble "can be boiled down to culture," adding that 50-person startups were getting products out faster than Intel.Transparency was the other big issue. According to Zinsner, information changed as it moved up the management chain, and by the time presentations reached the CEO, they often described a different situation from the one teams lower down knew about.He did not frame this as deliberate deception. Some managers simply did not want to admit a project was failing. The result was that Intel's top leadership sometimes made decisions based on an inaccurate picture of the business. Tan has since brought in executives he trusts who are used to working in leaner organisations.The VP cuts sit inside a much larger downsizing. Intel had 108,900 employees at the end of 2024 and 88,400 by late September 2025, including subsidiaries like Mobileye. Around 20,500 of those exits happened under Tan, who took charge in March 2025 and told staff there would be "no more blank checks." The pitch was about flattening management, but in Oregon only 8% of the laid-off employees had "manager" in their job titles. Most were engineers and technicians.Zinsner pointed to early signs of change. Several products have reached A-stepping, Intel's term for the first version of a chip, without the repeated development cycles that were once routine. Intel 18A yields are running ahead of internal milestones, and 14A defect density is tracking better than the company's target curve.Intel is now preparing for 14A risk production in 2027 and high-volume manufacturing in 2028. Internal product teams have started designing for the process, and interest from external foundry customers has picked up.Finances are moving too. Intel entered 2026 expecting gross margins in the high 30s and is now in the low 40s. The target is the mid-40s, then the high 40s, and eventually a figure starting with 5. To get there, Intel uses an internal "Rule of 45" that combines revenue growth and operating margin. Slower businesses must deliver stronger margins, while faster-growing ones can earn more investment.Halving the VP ranks gives Intel a leaner org chart, but the numbers Zinsner shared will only mean something if they hold. 14A is the first major process being developed entirely under Tan's structure, with fewer layers between engineers and the CEO and fewer people who can block a decision. If it reaches risk production in 2027 and volume manufacturing in 2028 as planned, it will be the clearest evidence yet that the cultural reset worked. If it slips into the multiple development cycles that marked the last decade, the 250 fewer vice presidents will have changed very little.
Article Summary: Intel has cut the number of vice presidents at the company from about 450 at its peak to roughly 200. It has also halved its management layers from 12 to six as CEO Lip-Bu Tan tries to get the chipmaker to decide faster and ship on time.Intel says 18A yields and 14A progress show the overhaul is working.

Article Title: Microsoft shakes up communications team; CEO Satya Nadella and President Brad Smith sends memo to employees, says 'We will likely have more employees and executives acting as ...'
Article Text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella described the communications shake-up as a response to a media environment

Why is Microsoft changing its communications strategy

Microsoft communications team will now report to Brad Smith

What happens to Microsoft communications chief Frank Shaw

Microsoft is changing how it communicates with the outside world. The company is moving its communications team out of its marketing organisation and into the corporate, external and legal affairs group led by Vice Chair and President Brad Smith, according to internal memos from Smith and CEO Satya Nadella . The bigger change, however, may be how Microsoft employees speak for the company. Nadella said the company wants engineers, sellers, partners and other employees who are close to its products and customers to play a bigger role in telling Microsoft's story.“We will likely have more employees and executives acting as part of Microsoft’s public voice, including on social media,” Smith wrote in his memo.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella described the communications shake-up as a response to a media environment that has become “increasingly fragmented and noisier than ever.” Instead of relying mainly on a central communications team to shape Microsoft's public messaging, the CEO wants people closer to the company's work to have a greater role.“In many ways, the people closest to the work have the best opportunity to shape how Microsoft is understood,” Nadella wrote. He said Microsoft wants engineers, sellers, partners and others “closest to our products and customers” to become “an even bigger part of how we tell our story, all connected by a shared strategy and set of principles.”Nadella added: “We will learn, we will experiment, and we will evolve. There is a fundamentally new way to think about communications, and this team will be central to building it.”Under the new structure, Microsoft's communications function will sit within the organisation led by President Brad Smith rather than under marketing. Smith's organisation handles Microsoft's legal, regulatory and public policy work, including antitrust matters, litigation and government relations.The communications team will therefore sit alongside these functions, although Microsoft plans to continue coordination between communications and marketing.Satya Nadella described Smith as one of the few Microsoft leaders who “embody Microsoft’s voice” authentically. He also praised Smith's “rare ability to communicate complex ideas with clarity, conviction, and trust.”The restructuring also changes the role of longtime Microsoft communications chief Frank X. Shaw. Shaw announced earlier this month that he would leave Microsoft at the end of the year after more than two decades with the company. He will now step away from his current responsibilities and serve as an adviser to Smith and interim communications leader Brent Colburn during the transition.Microsoft said Shaw will remain with the company through the end of the year. Shaw described the latest development as the formalisation of the plan that had already been announced.Microsoft said Shaw “has been a trusted counselor and leader at Microsoft for more than two decades, and we’re grateful he will continue to act as an advisor during the transition.”Satya Nadella also thanked Shaw for his contribution. He said Shaw has “made tremendous contributions to the company and to our communications function over the last 17+ years” and has been “a great source of counsel to our leadership team and to me personally, across the company’s biggest moments.”Smith also praised Shaw, saying he had “worked as closely with him as almost anyone” over the years. Smith added that Shaw's “enduring impact on Microsoft and this team will be felt for years to come. I will miss him.”
Article Summary: Microsoft is moving its communications team out of its marketing organisation and into the corporate, external and legal affairs group led by Vice Chair and President Brad Smith. The bigger change, however, may be how Microsoft employees speak for the company. Nadella said the company wants engineers, sellers, partners and other employees who are close to its products and customers to play a bigger role.

Article Title: Microsoft launches India South Central Cloud Hub in Telangana
Article Text:
Strategic infrastructure

Skilling for the datacenter economy

Water and sustainability

Microsoft has officially launched its India South Central cloud region in Hyderabad, Telangana, positioning it as a strategic hub for Asia and the Global South. Hon’ble Minister Shri D. Sridhar Babu joined Microsoft leaders for the inauguration, recognizing Telangana’s growing role in India’s cloud and AI economy. This marks Microsoft’s fourth cloud region in India, designed with a resilient three-zone architecture to meet rising demand for AI innovation and digital infrastructure.The India South Central region is now live and operational, serving customers across India and neighboring regions. Microsoft confirmed that the hub will support long-term capacity expansion, resilience, and AI innovation, with some of India’s most trusted institutions already building on it. The company emphasized that Hyderabad’s ecosystem of talent, academia, and industry will help power next-generation AI and cloud services not only for India but globally.•Resilient three-zone architecture for scalability and reliability.•Largest hyperscale cloud footprint in India, supporting AI-ready workloads.•Designed to serve Asia and the Global South, strengthening India’s position in global cloud infrastructure.Community development•Comprehensive Community Development Programme has reached over 22,400 people in Hyderabad’s datacenter region.•Entrepreneurship initiatives have supported 117 micro-enterprises, sustaining 129 families in Rangareddy district.•Focus on women-led businesses including tailoring, catering, and retail ventures.•Microsoft’s Data Center Academy partners with IIIT Hyderabad, Young India Skills University, Don Bosco Tech Society, and the Telangana government.•600-hour industry-aligned program prepares students for careers in datacenter operations.•Over 556 young people trained, with 118 securing placements; additional analytics programs trained 151 students with 108 placements.•Part of Microsoft’s wider goal to equip 20 million Indians with AI skills by 2030.•Operates with effectively zero water use for cooling, aligning with Microsoft’s global sustainability goals.•Local water resilience projects include groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting, and watershed management.•By June 2026, the Elikatta program added five million liters of recharge capacity.
Article Summary: The India South Central cloud region is now live and operational, serving customers across India and neighboring regions. Microsoft confirmed that the hub will support long-term capacity expansion, resilience, and AI innovation. The company emphasized that Hyderabad’s ecosystem of talent, academia, and industry will help power next-generation AI.

Article Title: Budget phones are disappearing fast, report says by 2030, 40% of sub-Rs 20,000 smartphones may be gone
Article Text:
Why budget phones’ shipment will squeeze

Smartphone shipment rebound expected through 2030

The era of the budget smartphones is rapidly shrinking. Over 230 million annual smartphone shipments priced below $200 (Rs 20,000) will vanish from worldwide retail channels between 2025 and 2030, a report has said. According to Counterpoint Research’s Smartphone Shipment Forecast by Price Band tracker, this segment will contract by roughly 40% through the end of the decade. The decline comes even as total worldwide smartphone shipments stage a broader rebound back toward 2025 volumes.The disappearing budget tier stems largely from structural aftershocks linked to the 2026–2027 industry downturn. A combination of rising prices for mobile chipsets and memory, higher baseline hardware requirements and phone makers scaling back unprofitable market footprints has made entry-level devices increasingly hard to sustain, the report said, adding, as components eat up a far larger share of total build costs on inexpensive devices, manufacturers have virtually no room to absorb price jumps.It also said that rather than buying brand-new budget handsets, consumers are responding in several ways. For example, users are delaying upgrades and extending how long they keep their existing devices. Some buyers are turning to certified refurbished and second-hand phones, and a portion of buyers is moving up into higher price tiers via installment plans.“The smartphone market will recover in unit terms, but the affordable segment will not return to its previous standing.The opportunity now shifts toward better-specced mainstream devices and premium products, although higher tiers cannot absorb all the lost volume. The result will be a market that is similar in overall size but materially different in value and competitive profile. There is also a wider connectivity risk, as the loss of affordable new smartphones could make it harder for first-time users in lower-income markets to come online,” said Yang Wang, Principal Analyst at Counterpoint Research.Counterpoint estimates that overall smartphone deliveries will climb back to approximately 1.20 billion units by 2030, just behind 2025 benchmark levels. The stagnation across the mid-range highlights that budget volume is not simply flowing upward in a straight line. Instead, delayed purchase cycles and disappearing first-time buyer demand mean higher tiers will not make up for all the lost volume under $200.Across developing and lower-income markets, device affordability remains the single greatest roadblock to mobile internet access. As sub-$200 options disappear, the transition from basic feature phones or shared family devices to personal smartphone ownership risks slowing to a crawl. This slowdown threatens to complicate long-term efforts by network operators, software developers, and governments seeking to broaden digital public infrastructure, localized content and mobile financial services.
Article Summary: Over 230 million annual smartphone shipments priced below $200 (Rs 20,000) will vanish from worldwide retail channels between 2025 and 2030. The disappearing budget tier stems largely from structural aftershocks linked to the 2026–2027 industry downturn. Counterpoint estimates that overall smartphone deliveries will climb back to approximately 1.20 billion units by 2030.

Article Title: Google, OpenAI and Anthropic may launch AI safety standard by early 2027
Article Text:
Momentum builds following safety proposals

Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are said to be collaborating to establish an independent artificial intelligence (AI) safety body by late 2026 or early 2027, a report from The Information has claimed, adding that they have reached out to former White House AI policy advisor Sriram Krishnan to serve as chief executive. The report says that the planned organisation, provisionally named the Standards Authority for Frontier AI (SAFA), will operate independently of government administration. Its primary mission will be to define practical benchmarks for the three companies' public safety pledges and provide direct support to developers evaluating cutting-edge models prior to commercial deployment.Citing people familiar with the initiative, the report said that apart from Krishnan, the companies have reached out to Arati Prabhakar, former director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, to take the top post at SAFA. The three technology giants are also weighing whether SAFA should conduct direct model assessments in-house.While the United States Center for AI Standards and Innovation already handles federal evaluation, insiders noted persistent concerns that the government agency lacks adequate technical and financial resources to thoroughly inspect complex frontier systems.The push toward a joint authority follows weeks of escalating industry dialogue.About 10 days ago, an OpenAI spokesperson confirmed to CNBC that the company was holding active talks with Google and Anthropic regarding coordinated safety frameworks. These discussions gained momentum following a proposal published on X in July by Sir Demis Hassabis, co-founder of Google DeepMind and Alphabet’s chief scientist. Hassabis argued for a US-backed standards body modeled after a public-private partnership or a self-regulatory watchdog, drawing comparisons to the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).While Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI remain locked in a race for commercial dominance, leadership across all three firms has faced mounting scrutiny over potential catastrophic and security risks. The momentum toward collective oversight accelerated earlier this month after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei released an essay calling for an industrywide slowdown in the release of frontier models to allow safety mechanisms to catch up.
Article Summary: Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are said to be collaborating to establish an independent artificial intelligence (AI) safety body by late 2026 or early 2027. The planned organisation, provisionally named the Standards Authority for Frontier AI (SAFA), will operate independently of government administration. Its primary mission will be to define practical benchmarks for the three companies' public safety pledges.
